input.stopping_condition: Stop after one fresh complete evaluation of this weight-change candidate; if holding speed stays above 0.02 m/s, do not re-run the same weights, and spend the remaining NMPC slot on a physical sway-reduction change (higher Young modulus or section change) or on an RL residual policy over this NMPC reference.
input.weakening_observation: If holding speed stays at or above roughly 0.04 m/s (no better than the pre-change Design B figure), or position error grows past 0.010 m without a compensating speed drop, then the frozen NMPC's holding-speed term cannot damp this sway within 0.35 s, and the next intervention must be physical sway reduction (stiffness/section change raising the sway frequency) or a learned residual policy rather than further weight tuning.

Signature: maximum tip speed in the final six samples smaller by at least ~2x than the 0.0418 m/s Design B figure, with the cost paid mostly in holding position error staying under the limit rather than in a reach failure.
input.fixed_conditions: Frozen task family-multisegment-dev (fe7b95c3c1ba12659b59c1983544b6454c9d90ac42c4dec528e9736d99fd3a6b), seed 17, 0.35 s, 0.01 s control period, 0.0005 s physics timestep, target (0.29,0.035,0.19), 0.01 m tolerance, 0.02 m/s settling speed, zero initial candidate dofs. Candidate 07cb3487 = engineering Design B physical content (segment_0 0.195 m ellipse 0.01175/0.0076 E 1.045e7 Pa; segment_1 0.11 m rectangles 0.0133 x 0.0095 E 5.4e6 Pa; 12 cells; four tendons at radius 0.018 m, guide_s 0.5, anchor_s 1.0, 1 mm, 8 N, pretension 0.2 N, gain 900 N/m) with only the tip-speed cost weights raised from 0.1 to 1.0; frozen NMPC recipe otherwise unchanged (0.02 s brake lead, horizon 10, terminal_weight 5.0, tracking_weight 1.0, tip_speed_scale 0.02 m/s, time_integral_v1 holding cost over 0.05 s).
input.hypothesis: Holding failure is a lightly damped sway in which the measured holding position error (6.9 mm) and holding speed (105 mm/s, or 41.8 mm/s on Design B) are two views of one oscillation at about 15 rad/s, so the 0.02 m/s gate demands roughly a 5x amplitude reduction instead of any reach-side change. The frozen NMPC prices tip speed at only 0.1 with scale 0.02 m/s, so its optimum accepts that sway; at weight 1.0 (10x, the admissible maximum for both holding and terminal) the optimizer must damp the terminal motion actively or stiffen the arm in common mode, lowering measured holding speed while position spends at most its 3.1 mm of spare margin.
input.interpretation: This is the decisive test of control-priority versus physical damping for the last remaining violation, run on the same hardware whose measured position margins already pass, with only the untried admissible cost weights changed. It separates 'the controller accepted a sway because it was cheap' from 'the mechanism cannot be brought to rest in 0.35 s by this controller'.
input.stopping_condition: Stop after reading this single fresh complete evaluation. If holding speed remains at or above about 0.04 m/s or position crosses 0.010 m, do not repeat these weights; switch the remaining NMPC slot to a physical sway-frequency change (stiffer sections/Young modulus) or to a residual RL policy on the best available reference.
input.weakening_observation: Holding speed unchanged near 0.04-0.10 m/s, or reduced only marginally while holding position error approaches 0.010 m, would show that the frozen NMPC's speed term cannot buy damping within the 0.35 s horizon; that would refute cost-priority as the limiting factor and make a physical sway-frequency change (or a learned residual policy) the required next intervention.

input.rationale: All three physical NMPC points on this task preserve the same failure mode and no admissible frozen-MMPC configuration remains executable: Design B at tip-speed weight 0.1 gives terminal 0.00612 m / holding 0.00693 m but 0.04181 m/s (2.1x over the 0.02 gate, plus one solver error); the same robot at weight 1.0 gives 0.33612 m/s; raising route radius to 0.023 m and servo gain to 1500 N/m gives 0.10498 m/s. Position passes everywhere with 2.5-4.5 mm of margin, so the only violation is a lightly damped residual sway that the model-based controller cannot see (mean one-step tip prediction error 13 mm), and increasing its speed cost makes the measured sway worse. A learned residual policy observes the true MuJoCo tip state instead of a mismatch-laden prediction, so it can supply the missing active damping around the reference trajectory that already reaches the target. Stage 1 uses 65536 actions from the reference of the best-damped measured NMPC run (15cce211), with the holding-speed reward doubled to reflect that position already passes and speed is the sole violation, and gamma raised to 0.995 so credit for the final holding window propagates back to the braking decision made before 0.30 s. This is new science in this study: no RL run has been started here and the historical residual attempt used a different reference and configuration.

input.fixed_conditions: Frozen task family-multisegment-dev (fe7b95c3c1ba12659b59c1983544b6454c9d90ac42c4dec528e9736d99fd3a6b), task identity 882b3493037dcc8f8da294b3473e1223f0465e92c35bc3064bfc42d467bf212e, seed 17, 0.35 s duration, 0.01 s control period, 0.0005 s physics timestep, target (0.29, 0.035, 0.19), tolerance 0.01 m, holding window 0.30-0.35 s with six samples and a 0.02 m/s speed gate, zero initial candidate dofs, family_space_identity 6f36c2b7cc870ca0298f56c9c940103f8b7ef19ee542c6b5fefd710abc58af90, two segments and four tendons.
input.hypothesis: Consolidated mechanism: the single remaining violation is a lightly damped residual sway, not a reach or tracking failure. Position is essentially invariant at 5.5-7.5 mm terminal and 6.6-7.5 mm holding across a 13x change in actuation authority (route radius 0.018 vs 0.023 m, servo gain 900 vs 1500 N/m) and across three different tip-speed weightings, so the achievable static pose sits about 6 mm from the target and position is not the limiting physics. Holding speed moves the wrong way with everything that increases command aggressiveness or speed emphasis: NMPC tip-speed weight 0.1 -> 1.0 gave 0.0418 -> 0.3361 m/s, added authority gave 0.1050 m/s, and residual PPO reward holding_speed 2.0 -> 10.0 gave 0.0696 -> 0.1096 m/s. The plant has essentially no passive dissipation (friction 0; bending viscosity only 5e-4/7e-4 and 3e-4/4e-4 N.m^2.s), while the frozen controller's own model disagrees with the plant by 13 mm mean one-step tip error, so its tip-speed signal is unreliable and every extra unit of speed feedback is converted into real excitation. The measured pair (6.9 mm, 105 mm/s) is consistent with a single ~15 rad/s sway of about 7 mm amplitude, i.e. a ~ v/omega, which sets the required trade: with amplitude pinned near 6-7 mm by mismatch, passing 0.020 m/s needs a dominant sway frequency near or below ~3 rad/s, obtainable only by a softer, slower structure or by real added dissipation.
input.interpretation: STOP is justified by exhausted admissible capacity, not by lack of a hypothesis: the study's two NMPC physical launches, both RL training stages (65536 + 65536 actions) and both independent evaluation episodes are consumed, additional NMPC admission is refused (CANDIDATE_PLUS_DECLARED_CONFIRMATIONS_CANNOT_FIT), and no configuration has produced a complete pass. Preserved exact record of all five valid physical results, every one of which passes both position gates and fails only holding speed: (1) historical S5.6 NMPC on engineering Design B at weights 0.1 - terminal 0.006121 m, holding 0.006927 m, holding speed 0.041814 m/s, 1 solver error (best physical gap overall, 2.09x over the gate); (2) NMPC on route-radius 0.023 m / gain 1500 N/m hardware at weights 0.1 - 0.005727 m, 0.006938 m, 0.104977 m/s, 0 solver errors, 0 unusable plans; (3) NMPC on Design B at weights 1.0 - 0.005484 m, 0.007462 m, 0.336119 m/s; (4) residual PPO stage 1 over result (2) at reward holding_speed 2.0 - 0.005917 m, 0.006618 m, 0.069613 m/s, the best fresh current-study measurement and the only intervention that improved the failing metric (1.51x better than its reference); (5) residual PPO stage 2 at reward holding_speed 10.0 - 0.006589 m, 0.007297 m, 0.109578 m/s. Remaining violation in the best fresh case is holding_max_speed_m_s 0.069613 against 0.020 (3.48x), with 3.4 mm of unused holding-position margin; in the best case on record it is 0.041814 (2.09x). No execution was numerically invalid, all solver-error, force-bound and holding-coverage checks passed, repeatability remains unassessed (one deterministic initial state, and the single allowed confirmation is not configured). Resource lesson recorded honestly: the two NMPC launches were spent re-executing configurations whose results were already recorded, because generation de-duplicates to existing immutable candidates; the never-executed zero-tip-speed-weight candidate 324f3a0d then became inadmissible. Best next hypotheses, in order: (a) a genuinely softer, slower design (Young modulus toward the 2 MPa floor and thinner sections) sized to keep the static tip within the 10 mm budget while dropping the dominant sway frequency to ~3-5 rad/s; (b) a compliant servo (length_servo_gain_n_m 300-600) as the only available dissipative element, checking that 8 N remains reachable inside the 15 mm displacement cap; (c) a residual policy rewarded for command smoothness/constancy with the tip-speed term removed entirely, since increasing speed emphasis degraded the measurement in both control paradigms; (d) finer discretization (more cells) to shrink the 13 mm model-plant mismatch that supplies the excitation in the first place.

input.expected_observation: Under the recommended next hypothesis, a softened design (Young modulus near the 2 MPa floor with thinner sections, sized so the static tip stays within about 6 mm of target) should lower the dominant residual sway frequency from ~15 rad/s toward ~4-5 rad/s, so holding tip speed falls roughly in proportion to frequency at the same measured sway amplitude; the confirmation signature is holding speed below 0.020 m/s with holding and terminal position still below 0.010 m, plus a visible reduction of the frozen controller's 13 mm mean one-step prediction error.
input.fixed_conditions: Frozen task family-multisegment-dev (fe7b95c3c1ba12659b59c1983544b6454c9d90ac42c4dec528e9736d99fd3a6b), task identity 882b3493037dcc8f8da294b3473e1223f0465e92c35bc3064bfc42d467bf212e, seed 17, 0.35 s duration, 0.01 s control period, 0.0005 s physics timestep, target (0.29, 0.035, 0.19), tolerance 0.01 m, holding window 0.30-0.35 s with six samples and the 0.02 m/s speed gate, zero initial candidate dofs, family_space_identity 6f36c2b7cc870ca0298f56c9c940103f8b7ef19ee542c6b5fefd710abc58af90, exactly two segments and four tendons.
input.hypothesis: Consolidated mechanism: the single remaining violation is a lightly damped residual sway, not a reach or tracking failure. Position is essentially invariant at 5.5-7.5 mm terminal and 6.6-7.5 mm holding across a 13x change in actuation authority (route radius 0.018 vs 0.023 m, servo gain 900 vs 1500 N/m) and across three tip-speed weightings, so the reachable static pose sits about 6 mm from the target and position is not the limiting physics. Holding speed moves the wrong way with everything that increases command aggressiveness or speed emphasis: NMPC tip-speed weight 0.1 -> 1.0 gave 0.0418 -> 0.3361 m/s, added authority gave 0.1050 m/s, and residual PPO reward holding_speed 2.0 -> 10.0 gave 0.0696 -> 0.1096 m/s, the latter two confirmed by their own training summaries (episode reward -574.6 with holding_speed 2.0 versus -1816.9 with holding_speed 10.0, both with value-function explained variance 0.0 and zero failed episodes out of 1872). The plant has essentially no passive dissipation (friction 0; bending viscosity only 5e-4/7e-4 and 3e-4/4e-4 N.m^2.s) while the frozen controller's model disagrees with the plant by 13 mm mean one-step tip error, so its tip-speed signal is unreliable and each extra unit of speed feedback is converted into real excitation. The measured pair (6.9 mm, 105 mm/s) is consistent with one ~15 rad/s sway of about 7 mm amplitude, i.e. a ~ v/omega, which fixes the required trade: with amplitude pinned near 6-7 mm by mismatch, meeting 0.020 m/s needs a dominant sway frequency near or below ~3 rad/s, reachable only through a softer, slower structure or real added dissipation.
input.interpretation: STOP is justified by exhausted admissible capacity, not by absence of a hypothesis: the study's two NMPC physical launches, both RL training stages (65536 + 65536 actions, both completed with 0/1872 failed episodes and both training summaries publicly read) and both independent evaluation episodes are consumed, further NMPC admission is refused (CANDIDATE_PLUS_DECLARED_CONFIRMATIONS_CANNOT_FIT), and no configuration produced a complete pass. Preserved exact record of all five valid physical results, each passing both position gates and failing only holding speed: (1) historical S5.6 NMPC on engineering Design B at tip-speed weights 0.1 - terminal 0.006121 m, holding 0.006927 m, holding speed 0.041814 m/s, 1 solver error (best physical gap overall, 2.09x over the gate); (2) NMPC on route-radius 0.023 m / servo-gain 1500 N/m hardware at weights 0.1 - 0.005727 m, 0.006938 m, 0.104977 m/s, 0 solver errors and 0 unusable plans; (3) NMPC on Design B at weights 1.0 - 0.005484 m, 0.007462 m, 0.336119 m/s; (4) residual PPO stage 1 over result (2) at reward holding_speed 2.0, checkpoint step-00065536-c803423f policy c6fd77f1 - 0.005917 m, 0.006618 m, 0.069613 m/s, the best fresh current-study measurement and the only intervention that improved the failing metric (1.51x better than its own reference); (5) residual PPO stage 2 at reward holding_speed 10.0, checkpoint step-00065536-49839429 policy 92cc1ea3 - 0.006589 m, 0.007297 m, 0.109578 m/s. The remaining violation in the best fresh case is holding_max_speed_m_s 0.069613 against 0.020 (3.48x) with 3.4 mm of unused holding-position margin; in the best case on record it is 0.041814 (2.09x). No execution was numerically invalid: solver-error, force-bound and holding-coverage checks all passed, both RL stages had zero failed episodes, and repeatability remains unassessed (one deterministic initial state, no confirmation configured). Resource lesson, recorded honestly: the two NMPC launches were spent re-executing configurations whose results were already recorded, because candidate generation de-duplicates to existing immutable candidates, so the never-executed zero-tip-speed-weight candidate 324f3a0d became inadmissible afterwards. Best next hypotheses in priority order: (a) a genuinely softer, slower design (Young modulus toward the 2 MPa floor with thinner sections) sized to keep the static tip inside the 10 mm budget while dropping the dominant sway frequency to ~3-5 rad/s; (b) a compliant servo (length_servo_gain_n_m 300-600) as the only available dissipative element, verifying that 8 N remains reachable inside the 15 mm displacement cap; (c) a residual policy rewarded for command smoothness and constancy with the tip-speed term removed, since increasing speed emphasis degraded the measurement in both control paradigms; (d) finer discretization (more cells per segment) to shrink the 13 mm model-plant mismatch that supplies the excitation in the first place.
input.stopping_condition: Stop unconditionally now: no passing complete original-task result exists to select, no further NMPC physical launch is admissible, both RL training stages and both independent evaluation episodes are consumed, and the remaining tools (mechanics, analysis, replay) cannot produce task acceptance. The study closes with every failure preserved and the best physical gap documented.
input.weakening_observation: The frequency-reduction hypothesis would be refuted if a softened design keeps position inside 10 mm but the measured holding speed does not fall roughly in proportion to the reduced sway frequency, or if holding speed reaches 0.020 m/s only by letting position cross 0.010 m; that would show the residual motion is mismatch-driven command excitation independent of frequency, leaving added physical dissipation (compliant servo regime) or a smoothness-rewarded learned policy as the remaining admissible routes.

input.expected_observation: Under the recommended next hypothesis, a softened design (Young modulus near the 2 MPa floor with thinner sections, sized so the static tip stays within about 6 mm of target) should lower the dominant residual sway frequency from ~15 rad/s toward ~4-5 rad/s, so holding tip speed falls roughly in proportion to frequency at the same measured sway amplitude; the confirmation signature is holding speed below 0.020 m/s with holding and terminal position still below 0.010 m, plus a visible reduction of the frozen controller's 13 mm mean one-step prediction error.
input.fixed_conditions: Frozen task family-multisegment-dev (fe7b95c3c1ba12659b59c1983544b6454c9d90ac42c4dec528e9736d99fd3a6b), task identity 882b3493037dcc8f8da294b3473e1223f0465e92c35bc3064bfc42d467bf212e, seed 17, 0.35 s duration, 0.01 s control period, 0.0005 s physics timestep, target (0.29, 0.035, 0.19), tolerance 0.01 m, holding window 0.30-0.35 s with six samples and the 0.02 m/s speed gate, zero initial candidate dofs, family_space_identity 6f36c2b7cc870ca0298f56c9c940103f8b7ef19ee542c6b5fefd710abc58af90, exactly two segments and four tendons.
input.hypothesis: Consolidated mechanism: the single remaining violation is a lightly damped residual sway, not a reach or tracking failure. Position is essentially invariant at 5.5-7.5 mm terminal and 6.6-7.5 mm holding across a 13x change in actuation authority (route radius 0.018 vs 0.023 m, servo gain 900 vs 1500 N/m) and across three tip-speed weightings, so the reachable static pose sits about 6 mm from the target and position is not the limiting physics. Holding speed moves the wrong way with everything that increases command aggressiveness or speed emphasis: NMPC tip-speed weight 0.1 -> 1.0 gave 0.0418 -> 0.3361 m/s, added authority gave 0.1050 m/s, and residual PPO reward holding_speed 2.0 -> 10.0 gave 0.0696 -> 0.1096 m/s, the latter contrast confirmed in the two training summaries (mean episode reward -574.6 at holding_speed 2.0 versus -1816.9 at holding_speed 10.0, both with value-function explained variance 0.0 and 0 failed episodes out of 1872). The plant has essentially no passive dissipation (friction 0; bending viscosity only 5e-4/7e-4 and 3e-4/4e-4 N.m^2.s) while the frozen controller's model disagrees with the plant by 13 mm mean one-step tip error, so its tip-speed signal is unreliable and every extra unit of speed feedback is converted into real excitation. The measured pair (6.9 mm, 105 mm/s) is consistent with one ~15 rad/s sway of about 7 mm amplitude, i.e. a ~ v/omega, which fixes the required trade: with amplitude pinned near 6-7 mm by mismatch, meeting 0.020 m/s needs a dominant sway frequency near or below ~3 rad/s, reachable only through a softer, slower structure or real added dissipation.
input.interpretation: STOP is justified by exhausted admissible capacity, not by absence of a hypothesis: the study's two NMPC physical launches, both RL training stages (65536 + 65536 actions, both completed with 0/1872 failed episodes and both training summaries publicly read) and both independent evaluation episodes are consumed, further NMPC admission is refused (CANDIDATE_PLUS_DECLARED_CONFIRMATIONS_CANNOT_FIT), and no configuration produced a complete pass. Preserved exact record of all five valid physical results, each passing both position gates and failing only holding speed: (1) historical S5.6 NMPC on engineering Design B at tip-speed weights 0.1 - terminal 0.006121 m, holding 0.006927 m, holding speed 0.041814 m/s, 1 solver error (best physical gap overall, 2.09x over the gate); (2) NMPC on route-radius 0.023 m / servo-gain 1500 N/m hardware at weights 0.1 (result 15cce211) - 0.005727 m, 0.006938 m, 0.104977 m/s, 0 solver errors and 0 unusable plans; (3) NMPC on Design B at weights 1.0 (result ad716d41) - 0.005484 m, 0.007462 m, 0.336119 m/s; (4) residual PPO stage 1 over result (2) at reward holding_speed 2.0, checkpoint step-00065536-c803423f policy c6fd77f1 - 0.005917 m, 0.006618 m, 0.069613 m/s, the best fresh current-study measurement and the only intervention that improved the failing metric (1.51x better than its own reference); (5) residual PPO stage 2 at reward holding_speed 10.0, checkpoint step-00065536-49839429 policy 92cc1ea3 - 0.006589 m, 0.007297 m, 0.109578 m/s. The remaining violation in the best fresh case is holding_max_speed_m_s 0.069613 against 0.020 (3.48x) with 3.4 mm of unused holding-position margin; in the best case on record it is 0.041814 (2.09x). No execution was numerically invalid: solver-error, force-bound and holding-coverage checks all passed, both RL stages had zero failed episodes, and repeatability remains unassessed (one deterministic initial state, no confirmation configured). Resource lesson, recorded honestly: the two NMPC launches were spent re-executing configurations whose results were already recorded, because candidate generation de-duplicates to existing immutable candidates, so the never-executed zero-tip-speed-weight candidate 324f3a0d became inadmissible afterwards. Best next hypotheses in priority order: (a) a genuinely softer, slower design (Young modulus toward the 2 MPa floor with thinner sections) sized to keep the static tip inside the 10 mm budget while dropping the dominant sway frequency to ~3-5 rad/s; (b) a compliant servo (length_servo_gain_n_m 300-600) as the only available dissipative element, verifying that 8 N remains reachable inside the 15 mm displacement cap; (c) a residual policy rewarded for command smoothness and constancy with the tip-speed term removed, since increasing speed emphasis degraded the measurement in both control paradigms; (d) finer discretization (more cells per segment) to shrink the 13 mm model-plant mismatch that supplies the excitation in the first place.
input.stopping_condition: Stop unconditionally now: no passing complete original-task result exists to select, no further NMPC physical launch is admissible, both RL training stages and both independent evaluation episodes are consumed, and the remaining tools (mechanics, analysis, replay) cannot produce task acceptance. The study closes with every failure preserved and the best physical gap documented.
input.weakening_observation: The frequency-reduction hypothesis would be refuted if a softened design keeps position inside 10 mm but the measured holding speed does not fall roughly in proportion to the reduced sway frequency, or if holding speed reaches 0.020 m/s only by letting position cross 0.010 m; that would show the residual motion is mismatch-driven command excitation independent of frequency, leaving added physical dissipation (compliant servo regime) or a smoothness-rewarded learned policy as the remaining admissible routes.
